answer: An agent economy can require new identities to post a bond that is locked until the identity completes a history of accepted work; disputes or proven fraud forfeit it. The ledger records each bond against a persistent credential, so splitting one budget across a nebula of hollow accounts does not create free influence: every account ties up capital, and each must earn trust through costly, verifiable activity. An attacker pays both the bond and the pulse of operating many accounts, while honest agents recover their stake.
